name: Loktak Lake
summary: India's largest freshwater lake in the Northeast, known for floating phumdis and the Sangai deer habitat at Keibul Lamjao. Best experienced with a local boat operator; confirm timings and prices directly before travel.
tagline: A floating world of phumdis on the Northeast’s largest lake.

claims.valueText: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India with floating phumdis.

photos.caption: Boats on Loktak Lake, the floating lake
photos.attribution: © Haoreima, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Inland waterway activity on the lake
photos.attribution: © Haoreima, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
summary: The world's only floating national park, on Loktak Lake, and the last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer. Entry rules and sightings vary — check current guidance with officials or your host.
tagline: The world’s only floating national park, home of the Sangai.

claims.valueText: Only floating national park; last habitat of the Sangai deer.

photos.caption: Meitei cultural illustration of the Sangai deer (artwork, not a park photo)
Sangai antler reference diagram (illustration, not a park photo)

name: Sendra Resort
summary: Lakeside stay with panoramic phumdi views near Moirang. Official directory lists 13 rooms; current availability unconfirmed — always ask for your exact dates.
tagline: Lakeside rooms with panoramic phumdi views near Moirang.

claims.valueText: 13 rooms

photos.caption: Loktak Lake view (Sendra area lake view, not the resort building)

name: Kangla Fort
summary: Ancient seat of Meitei rulers in the heart of Imphal, with holy ponds, ruins and a museum. Holds deep historical and spiritual significance; confirm opening hours before visiting.
tagline: Two millennia of Meitei royalty in the heart of Imphal.

claims.valueText: Traditional seat of Manipuri rulers until 1891; archaeological site.

photos.caption: Traditional Meitei garden inside Kangla Fort
photos.attribution: © Haoreima, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Heikol Leikol garden, Kangla Palace grounds
photos.attribution: © Haoreima, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Ima Keithel
summary: The world's largest all-women-run market, where thousands of Imas sell handlooms, produce and crafts. Go with time to browse and cash in hand; ask stallholders before photographing.
tagline: Five thousand women vendors. One unforgettable market.

claims.valueText: All-women market with 3000+ vendors selling handlooms and produce.

photos.caption: Chak-hao black rice and Meitei Cheng in traditional Thumok baskets (market produce)
photos.attribution: © Haoreima, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Ima Market, Imphal
photos.attribution: © Ppyoonus, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: INA Memorial Complex
summary: Historic site in Moirang where the INA hoisted the tricolour in 1944, with a war museum. A solemn stop for history travellers on the lake circuit.
tagline: Where the tricolour first rose over India in 1944.

claims.valueText: Site of first INA flag hoisting on Indian soil (1944); war museum.

photos.caption: INA Memorial, Moirang
photos.attribution: © Ppyoonus, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: INA Memorial grounds, Moirang
photos.attribution: © Ppyoonus, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Shirui Kashong Peak
summary: High peak above Ukhrul, exclusive home of the rare Shirui Lily which blooms around May–June. Trek conditions and festival dates change yearly — verify the current edition before planning around it.
tagline: A lily that blooms nowhere else on Earth.

claims.valueText: Endemic habitat of the Shirui Lily; peak height 2835 m.

photos.caption: Hilltop village landscape, Ukhrul hills (representative scenery)

photos.caption: Wild lily bloom in the hills — Shirui Lily blooms May–June (Dzukou Lily pictured)
photos.attribution: © Gannu03, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Dzukou Valley
summary: Green valley meadows on the Manipur–Nagaland border, popular for multi-day treks. Access, permits and trail state vary by season — confirm with local guides and never trek alone without informing someone.
tagline: Emerald meadows straddling the Manipur–Nagaland hills.

claims.valueText: Border valley trekking meadows between Manipur and Nagaland.

photos.caption: Dzukou Valley on the Manipur–Nagaland border
photos.attribution: © UnpetitproleX, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

photos.caption: Dzukou Lily bloom in season
photos.attribution: © Gannu03, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple
summary: Historic Vaishnavite golden twin-domed temple adjacent to the palace of former Manipur Maharajas, celebrated for devotional rituals and classical Raas Leela performances.
tagline: Golden twin domes and the sacred heart of classical Raas Leela.

claims.valueText: Center of Vaishnavite culture and sacred classical dance in Manipur.

name: Shaheed Minar
summary: Tall commemorative obelisk standing in Bir Tikendrajit Park, honouring Meitei and tribal martyrs who fought valiantly in the 1891 Anglo-Manipur War.
tagline: A soaring tribute to the martyrs of the 1891 Anglo-Manipur War.

claims.valueText: Memorial obelisk honoring martyrs of the Anglo-Manipur War.

name: Mutua Bahadur Cultural Museum
summary: Open-air cultural complex in Andro showcasing authentic Meitei thatched architecture, wood carvings, tribal relics, and ancient pottery traditions.
tagline: An open-air living archive of indigenous art, craft, and architecture.

claims.valueText: Cultural museum presenting indigenous tribal architecture and pottery.

name: Imphal War Cemetery
summary: Peacefully maintained Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery holding the graves of 1,600 soldiers who fell during the decisive 1944 Battle of Imphal.
tagline: Quiet lawns remembering the decisive Allied battleground of WWII.

claims.valueText: Commonwealth memorial ground for 1,600 soldiers of WWII Battle of Imphal.

name: Red Hill & India Peace Memorial
summary: Historical battle site on Maibam Lotpa Ching hill where intense hand-to-hand combat took place in 1944; home to the Japan-built India Peace Memorial.
tagline: Where history turned in 1944 — now a solemn monument of world peace.

claims.valueText: Historic WWII Battle of Red Hill site with Japan-built peace memorial.

name: Khongjom War Memorial Complex
summary: Monument complex atop Kheba Ching hill where Paona Brajabasi and fellow warriors fought heroically to the last breath against the British Army in April 1891.
tagline: The historic hill of bravery and the last stand of the Meitei kingdom.

claims.valueText: Site of the Anglo-Manipur War 1891 where Major Paona Brajabasi fell.

name: Andro Heritage Village
summary: Centuries-old craft settlement famed for hand-coiled pottery (charpu), local distillation traditions, and the sacred perpetually burning fire of deity Panam Ningthou.
tagline: Ancient coil pottery and a sacred flame burning across centuries.

claims.valueText: Centuries-old heritage village with eternal fire and traditional coil pottery.

name: Kaina Sacred Hillock
summary: Sacred wooded hillock surrounded by jackfruit trees where King Bhagyachandra was divinely inspired to carve the revered idol of Lord Govindajee.
tagline: Wooded hills of divine vision and the origin of Lord Govindajee.

claims.valueText: Sacred place associated with King Bhagyachandra's vision of Lord Govindajee.

name: Bijoy Govindaji Temple
summary: Historic temple in Sagolband central to the annual Heikru Hidongba boat race festival on its ceremonial moat, steeped in 18th-century court history.
tagline: Historic shrine and home of the ceremonial Heikru Hidongba boat race.

claims.valueText: Historical temple venue for annual Heikru Hidongba traditional boat festival.

name: Khangkhui Mangsor Lime Caves
summary: Prehistoric limestone cave system with spacious calcified halls dating back to the Paleolithic Stone Age, nestled amidst Ukhrul's pine-carpeted slopes.
tagline: Prehistoric limestone chambers carved out in the Paleolithic dawn.

claims.valueText: Paleolithic archaeological limestone cave in Ukhrul district.

name: Tharon Cave
summary: A 655-meter subterranean limestone labyrinth featuring intricate natural tunnels, underground streams, and Hobinhian Stone Age archaeological excavations.
tagline: An underground limestone labyrinth echoing with Hobinhian antiquity.

claims.valueText: Prehistoric 655-meter cave system linked to ancient Southeast Asian stone culture.

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall
summary: Perennial three-tiered cascade plunging through lush tropical vegetation and rock ravines, one of Manipur's favorite weekend day-trek destinations.
tagline: Three cascading tiers tumbling through cool subtropical rainforest.

claims.valueText: Picturesque three-stage cascade nestled in the Leimaram valley.

name: Seven Barak Waterfalls
summary: Series of seven dramatic waterfalls roaring along the wild Barak River course amidst untouched evergreen rainforests and rich avian biodiversity.
tagline: Seven untamed cascades coursing through virgin rainforest canyons.

claims.valueText: Series of seven majestic cascades on the Barak River in Tamenglong.

name: Zeilad Lake Sanctuary
summary: Pristine high-altitude wetland surrounded by six associated sister lakes and dense jungle, famous for migratory winter birds, pythons, and tribal folklore.
tagline: High-altitude lake haven shrouded in mystery, birds, and virgin green.

claims.valueText: Protected natural wetland sanctuary known for migratory bird stopovers.

name: Khonghampat Orchidarium
summary: State botanical reserve spanning 200 acres that preserves more than 110 rare species of orchids, creating a riot of blossoms during spring (March to May).
tagline: Two hundred acres of indigenous forest sheltering over 110 orchid species.

claims.valueText: Botanical reserve preserving rare indigenous orchid flora of Northeast India.

name: Marjing Polo Complex
summary: Hilltop monument featuring a colossal 122-foot bronze statue of a polo player riding a Manipuri pony, honoring Manipur as the cradle of modern polo.
tagline: The 122-foot polo colossus celebrating Manipur as the birthplace of polo.

claims.valueText: World's tallest polo player statue honoring Sagol Kangjei heritage.

name: Kakching Garden
summary: Scenic hilltop garden atop Uyok Ching hill featuring terraced flower gardens, scenic valley gazebos, cultural statues, and an ancient Shiva temple.
tagline: Terraced floral hilltops looking out across the southern valley plains.

claims.valueText: Landscaped hillside botanical retreat and regional cultural landmark.

name: Santhei Natural Park
summary: Community-conserved eco-park surrounding a crystal-clear artificial reservoir at the base of Andro hills, framed by forested pines and picnic glades.
tagline: Crystal reservoir reflections framed by pine groves and Andro foothills.

claims.valueText: Community-managed eco-tourism park and artificial reservoir in Andro.

name: Takmu Water Sports Complex
summary: State-of-the-art watersports training and recreational hub situated on Takmu Lake (an arm of Loktak), hosting canoeing, kayaking, and rowing activities.
tagline: Water racing across calm lake channels beneath forested hill ranges.

claims.valueText: Regional hub for aquatic sports including canoeing and kayaking.

name: Singda Dam
summary: The world's highest mud-and-rock earthen dam, perched at 920 meters altitude, offering cool highland breezes, trekking paths, and peaceful reservoir panoramas.
tagline: The world’s highest earthen dam cradled by quiet mist-laden hills.

claims.valueText: World's highest earthen dam situated at 920 meters elevation.
